# SMF type 113 field reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_smf113_fields_doc.py from src/smfparser/records/type113.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

SMF type 113 is written by HIS (hardware instrumentation services) with the CPU-measurement
facility counters of each logical processor, once per collection interval (SMFINTVAL). The
counters show how a processor spends its cycles, e.g. cycles per instruction (CPI) and cache
behaviour, and are the input for capacity planning metrics such as RNI.

| Subtype | Table | Contents |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | `smf113_1` | One row per CPU per interval. Counter **deltas** since the previous record (IBM recommends this subtype) |
| 2 | `smf113_2` | One row per CPU per interval. **Absolute** counter values since the counters were enabled; basic, problem-state, crypto and extended sets only |
| 1 | `smf113_1_counters` | One row per counter; only with `records: {113: {counters: true}}` |
| 2 | `smf113_2_counters` | One row per counter; only with `records: {113: {counters: true}}` |

Column names are the IBM field names in lower case. The layout follows the z/OS 2.5 SMF manual and
was checked against z/OS 2.5 records from a z15. Both subtypes were compared with EPV's decoding of
the same dump (all EPV columns match).

**Things to know**
- The TOD-clock times (`smf113intervalstart`/`end`, `smf113_x_cts`/`ctm`) are UTC in the record.
  They are shifted to local time, so they line up with `smf_datetime`. The offset is taken from
  the record time minus SMF113_x_CTM, which are less than a second apart.
- Subtype 2 counters are cumulative: subtract the previous record of the same CPU (and the same run,
  `smf113_2_cts`) to get an interval's value. Subtype 1 already holds the deltas.
- A counter that is empty (NULL) was not recorded. A zero counter was recorded but the event did not
  happen (or isn't defined on this machine).

## Common header columns

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `source_file` | string | Path of the dump file the record came from |
| `record_offset` | Int64 | Byte offset in the file of the record's first segment (with `source_file`, a unique row key) |
| `smf_datetime` | datetime64[us] | Time and date the record was written (SMF113TME + SMF113DTE), local time: just after the end of the interval |
| `smf_type` | Int64 | Record type (SMF113RTY): 113 |
| `smf_subtype` | Int64 | Record subtype (SMF113STY): 1 counter deltas, 2 absolute counters |
| `smf_sid` | string | System identifier (SMF113SID) |
| `smf_ssi` | string | Subsystem identifier (SMF113WID), `HIS` |
| `smf_flag` | Int64 | Header flag byte (SM113FLG) |

## Subsystem section

Located by the SMF113SOF triplet. Offsets are from the start of the section.

| Column | Offset | Len | Type | Description |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `smf113rvn` | 2 | 2 | text (EBCDIC) | Record version number |
| `smf113pnm` | 4 | 8 | text (EBCDIC) | Product name (`HIS`) |
| `smf113osl` | 12 | 8 | text (EBCDIC) | MVS product level, e.g. `SP7.2.5` |

## Identification section

Located by the SMF113IOF triplet.

| Column | Offset | Len | Type | Description |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `smf113jbn` | 0 | 8 | text (EBCDIC) | Job name of the HIS address space |
| `smf113rsd` | 12 | 4 | date | Reader start date of the HIS address space |
| `smf113rst` | 8 | 4 | datetime | Reader start time of the HIS address space |
| `smf113stp` | 16 | 8 | text (EBCDIC) | Step name |
| `smf113intervalstart` | 24 | 8 | datetime | Interval start, shifted from UTC to local time |
| `smf113intervalend` | 32 | 8 | datetime | Interval end, shifted from UTC to local time |

## Subtype 1 data section (`smf113_1` only)

Located by the SMF113DOF triplet. The counter set triplet (SMF113_1_CSOF) is not written as columns.

| Column | Offset | Len | Type | Description |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `smf113_1_cts` | 0 | 8 | datetime | Start of the hardware data collection run (HIS start), local time |
| `smf113_1_ctm` | 8 | 8 | datetime | Time the counters were read for this record, local time |
| `smf113_1_cpuid` | 16 | 2 | integer | Logical processor ID the counters are for (0 is valid) |
| `smf113_1_cpuprocclass` | 18 | 1 | integer | Processor type: 0 CP, 2 zAAP, 4 zIIP (also in `cpu_type`) |
| `smf113_1_cpuspeed` | 20 | 4 | integer | Processor speed, cycles per microsecond |
| `smf113_1_machtype` | 24 | 4 | text (EBCDIC) | Machine type, e.g. `8561` (z15) |
| `smf113_1_machmodel` | 28 | 16 | text (EBCDIC) | Machine model, e.g. `T01` |
| `smf113_1_ctrversion0` | 44 | 2 | integer | z/OS counter set version |
| `smf113_1_ctrversion1` | 46 | 2 | integer | Basic and problem-state counter set version (CFVN) |
| `smf113_1_ctrversion2` | 48 | 2 | integer | Crypto, extended and MT-diagnostic counter set version (CSVN); identifies the machine generation whose extended counter definitions apply |
| `smf113_1_flags` | 50 | 2 | integer | Flags: 0x8000 the hardware lost counter data during the interval, 0x4000 it lost MT counter data |
| `smf113_1_machseqcode` | 60 | 16 | text (EBCDIC) | Machine sequence (serial) code |
| `smf113_1_coreid` | 76 | 2 | integer | Core ID the counters are for (core counter sets are recorded from one CPU per core) |

## Subtype 2 data section (`smf113_2` only)

Located by the SMF113DOF triplet. The counter set and counter triplets and the deprecated
`SMF113_2_CPU#` are not written as columns.

| Column | Offset | Len | Type | Description |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `smf113_2_cts` | 0 | 8 | datetime | Start of the hardware data collection run (HIS start), local time |
| `smf113_2_ctm` | 8 | 8 | datetime | Time the counters were read for this record, local time |
| `smf113_2_cpuprocclass` | 17 | 1 | integer | Processor type: 0 CP, 2 zAAP, 4 zIIP (also in `cpu_type`) |
| `smf113_2_cf` | 18 | 2 | integer | Flags: 0x8000 first record of the run (initial values), 0x4000 intermediate, 0x2000 final, 0x1000 non-standard hardware, 0x0800 the hardware lost counter data |
| `smf113_2_ctrvn1` | 20 | 2 | integer | Basic and problem-state counter set version (CFVN) |
| `smf113_2_ctrvn2` | 22 | 2 | integer | Crypto and extended counter set version (CSVN) |
| `smf113_2_cpsp` | 40 | 4 | integer | Processor speed, cycles per microsecond |
| `smf113_2_machtype` | 44 | 4 | text (EBCDIC) | Machine type, e.g. `8561` (z15) |
| `smf113_2_machmodel` | 48 | 16 | text (EBCDIC) | Machine model, e.g. `T01` |
| `smf113_2_cpuid` | 64 | 2 | integer | Logical processor ID the counters are for (0 is valid) |
| `smf113_2_machseqcode` | 68 | 16 | text (EBCDIC) | Machine sequence (serial) code |

## Counter columns

Both tables have the same counter columns, named `<set>_<counter number>`. The counter number is the
CPU-measurement facility number (first counter of each set + slot), so `basic_1` is counter 1 and
`extended_128` is counter 128. Counters are 8-byte unsigned integers (subtype 1 can also record
4-byte ones).

| Set | Columns | Counter numbers | Subtype |
|---|---|---|---|
| Basic (1) | `basic_0` … `basic_5` | 0–5 | 1, 2 |
| Problem-state (2) | `problem_32` … `problem_37` | 32–37 | 1, 2 |
| Crypto-activity (3) | `crypto_64` … `crypto_83` | 64–83 | 1, 2 |
| Extended (4) | `extended_128` … `extended_287` | 128–287 | 1, 2 |
| MT-diagnostic (6) | `mtdiag_448` … `mtdiag_463` | 448–463 | 1 only |

The z/OS counter set (type 5) has no counter numbers and is only in the counters table. Counters past
the columns above are only in the counters table too (a warning is logged once).

The **extended** counters depend on the machine generation (`smf113_x_ctrversion2` / `ctrvn2`).
Their meaning is listed per machine in IBM's *The CPU-Measurement Facility Extended Counters
Definition for z10, z196/z114, zEC12/zBC12, z13/z13s, z14, z15 and z16* (SA23-2261).

The others are architected:

| Counter | Column | Meaning |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | `basic_0` | Cycle count |
| 1 | `basic_1` | Instruction count |
| 2 | `basic_2` | L1 I-cache directory-write count |
| 3 | `basic_3` | L1 I-cache penalty cycle count |
| 4 | `basic_4` | L1 D-cache directory-write count |
| 5 | `basic_5` | L1 D-cache penalty cycle count |
| 32 | `problem_32` | Problem-state cycle count |
| 33 | `problem_33` | Problem-state instruction count |
| 34 | `problem_34` | Problem-state L1 I-cache directory-write count |
| 35 | `problem_35` | Problem-state L1 I-cache penalty cycle count |
| 36 | `problem_36` | Problem-state L1 D-cache directory-write count |
| 37 | `problem_37` | Problem-state L1 D-cache penalty cycle count |
| 448 | `mtdiag_448` | MT-diagnostic: cycles with one thread active |
| 449 | `mtdiag_449` | MT-diagnostic: cycles with two threads active |
| 64 | `crypto_64` | PRNG function count |
| 65 | `crypto_65` | PRNG cycle count |
| 66 | `crypto_66` | PRNG blocked function count |
| 67 | `crypto_67` | PRNG blocked cycle count |
| 68 | `crypto_68` | SHA function count |
| 69 | `crypto_69` | SHA cycle count |
| 70 | `crypto_70` | SHA blocked function count |
| 71 | `crypto_71` | SHA blocked cycle count |
| 72 | `crypto_72` | DEA function count |
| 73 | `crypto_73` | DEA cycle count |
| 74 | `crypto_74` | DEA blocked function count |
| 75 | `crypto_75` | DEA blocked cycle count |
| 76 | `crypto_76` | AES function count |
| 77 | `crypto_77` | AES cycle count |
| 78 | `crypto_78` | AES blocked function count |
| 79 | `crypto_79` | AES blocked cycle count |
| 80 | `crypto_80` | ECC function count |
| 81 | `crypto_81` | ECC cycle count |
| 82 | `crypto_82` | ECC blocked function count |
| 83 | `crypto_83` | ECC blocked cycle count |

For example, cycles per instruction (CPI) for each CPU and interval:

```sql
SELECT smf113intervalend, smf113_1_cpuid, cpu_type, 1.0 * basic_0 / basic_1 AS cpi
FROM smf113_1
ORDER BY smf113intervalend, smf113_1_cpuid;
```

## Derived columns

Computed by smfparser; last in every row.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cpu_type` | string | Processor type from SMF113_x_CpuProcClass: `CP`, `zAAP` or `zIIP` |
| `duration_sec` | Float64 | Interval length in seconds: SMF113IntervalEnd − SMF113IntervalStart |

## Counters tables: `smf113_1_counters`, `smf113_2_counters`

One row per counter of each record, written only with the `counters` option. They hold every
counter, including the z/OS set and counters past the counter columns. `source_file` +
`record_offset` join back to `smf113_1` / `smf113_2`.

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `source_file` | string | Copied from the record |
| `record_offset` | Int64 | Copied from the record |
| `smf_datetime` | datetime64[us] | Copied from the record |
| `smf_sid` | string | Copied from the record |
| `cpu_type` | string | Copied from the record |
| `smf113intervalstart` | datetime64[us] | Copied from the record |
| `smf113intervalend` | datetime64[us] | Copied from the record |
| `cpu_id` | Int64 | SMF113_x_CpuId |
| `counter_set` | string | `basic`, `problem`, `crypto`, `extended`, `zos` or `mtdiag` |
| `counter_index` | Int64 | Slot of the counter within its set, from 0 |
| `counter_number` | Int64 | CPU-measurement facility counter number; empty for the z/OS set |
| `counter_value` | Int64 | The counter: a delta (subtype 1) or an absolute value (subtype 2) |
